description:

covered lines above the 80% threshold. The buffer is dangerously thin: a single
bad merge could drop us below the gate.

This item systematically brings the 25 lowest-coverage modules up to ≥80% each,
adding robustness to the overall coverage floor and reducing the risk of accidental
regression below the gate.

Root cause: the original work units under-estimated the number of new covered
lines required. Large adapter modules (bigquery, redshift, databricks, snowflake)
have deep call trees with many branches that need dedicated test scenarios for
each path through connection setup, data loading, query execution, SQL generation,
and tuning application.

Additional work units w15-w24 added below to close the remaining ~1,744 lines
of coverage gap across the 19 modules that haven't yet reached 80%.
Combined with w3 (~322 lines), total remaining work is ~2,066 new covered lines.

All tests MUST carry the @pytest.mark.fast marker so they run in the fast lane.
All external SDKs (databricks, pyspark, snowflake-connector, boto3, google-cloud,
pyodbc, duckdb, requests) are mocked - no live connections.

anti_patterns.why: those markers cause tests to be excluded from the fast lane and won't count toward the 80% coverage gate

anti_patterns.dont: batch all 25 modules into a single test file
anti_patterns.instead: keep per-module or per-group test files aligned with existing test directory structure
anti_patterns.why: monolithic test files make coverage diffs unreadable and slow down targeted reruns

anti_patterns.dont: call list() on color_cycle() return values
anti_patterns.why: color_cycle() returns an infinite itertools.cycle; use list(theme.palette or DEFAULT_PALETTE) instead

anti_patterns.dont: import or instantiate real cloud SDK clients in tests
anti_patterns.instead: mock all external SDK calls with unittest.mock.patch
anti_patterns.why: CI has no cloud credentials and live calls cause flakiness and violate the fast-lane contract

anti_patterns.dont: modify production source files to make them more testable
anti_patterns.why: changes to production code require their own review cycle and could introduce regressions that dwarf the coverage gain
this strips -n auto and makes tests 10x slower

preserves.behavior: @pytest.mark.fast marker present on every new test function
All existing passing tests continue to pass - zero regressions
No live network calls - all external SDK clients mocked with unittest.mock.patch
No production source files modified - tests only
Overall fast-lane coverage stays ≥80.04% after every individual work unit commit
